newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan seen buying more US car parts amid trade gap.
newsitem.headline: Japan seen buying more US car parts amid trade gap.

text.p: Japan bought a record amount of U.S.-made car parts in the past business year, and analysts said the number was sure to rise as tension mounted over Japan's huge trade surplus.

The Japan Automobile Manufacturers Association (JAMA) said on Thursday that purchases of U.S. car parts by Japanese vehicle makers rose to a record $22.74 billion in the year to March 1997, up 8.1 percent from the previous record of $21.03 billion in 1995/96.

"Imports were only a drop in the bucket compared with Japan's huge exports to the United States. The U.S. is likely to demand that Japan boost its imports," said Koji Endo, a senior vice president at Lehman Brothers Japan Inc.
Of Japan's total purchase of U.S.-made car parts, imports for use at plants in Japan totalled $3.69 billion, up 9.2 percent, JAMA said.
Seiji Sugiura, a car industry analyst at Nomura Securities Co Ltd's research unit, agreed with Endo that Washington is likely to put pressure on Tokyo to do more to boost imports.

The U.S. Commerce Department said in June that the U.S. deficit with Japan grew by 5.1 percent to $4.84 billion in April. Japan also said in June that its merchandise trade surplus with the United States surged 93 percent in May from a year earlier to 322.87 billion yen ($2.83 billion).

Booming car exports have been a key factor in pushing up Japan's trade surplus, whose growth has dismayed key trading partners such as the United States and drawn increasingly tough warnings of a possible trade war.

According to the industry association's data, Japan's overall vehicle exports, including car parts, fell 1.2 percent from a year earlier to $78.34 billion in 1996/97. But Japan's exports have recently been on the rise, posting 4.5 percent and 7.7 percent gains in value terms in April and May respectively.
Japan's vehicle exports to the United States have been rising since June last year.

U.S. President Bill Clinton said on June 22 after the Group of Seven (G7) industrialised nations' summit in Denver, Colorado that Japan was risking an economic war with the United States if its trade surplus started exploding again.

"Because of a view that GM (General Motors Corp) is likely to revise down its business in the second quarter and due to poor sales of American cars in Japan, there is likely to be pressure from the U.S. in October when the Clinton administration is expected to report whether there has been progress in opening up the market as stated in the 1996 car trade deal with Japan," Nomura's Sugiura said.

As the business of U.S. carmakers is likely to start worsening from the third quarter of 1997, U.S. carmakers may step up their criticism of Japanese trade practices by the end of this year to curb Japanese exports, Endo said.

"Japan's purchases of U.S.- and EU-made car parts are likely to increase further in view of rising production by Japanese car makers in the United States and Europe and their plans to increase the variety of products there," a JAMA official said. ($1=114 yen)
